title: Pilot iteration 3: TTFT & streaming review
transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date: 2025-05-06
- Start time: 15:00 PT
- Duration: ~52 minutes
- Recording ID: ff-20250506-8392
- Documents shared: pilot-results-v3.xlsx (link), redwood-ttft-tuning-notes.pdf (link), kernel-profiles.csv (link)

Summary (auto): quick run through of iteration 3 results focused on TTFT improvements and streaming behavior. Discussed kernel switch, sequence-length trimming, and prefix caching. Agreed on next steps: Owen to hand off tuned container config, Maya to send revised committed capacity quote, Trajecta to run internal service-level test and share logs.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Maya from Redwood, I'm joined by Owen and Daria. How's the signal on your side?
[00:08] Lena Ortiz: Good morning, yeah signal's fine, we've got Markus and Priya here as well. Evan may drop in a bit.
[00:12] Owen Patel: Cool. We'll keep it focused — we've got the v3 numbers to go over and a couple of config recs.
[00:22] Maya Chen: Quick agenda — one, run through the TTFT numbers for the model slice you shipped; two, streaming behavior and token-first-turn time (TTFT) improvements; three, kernel choices and sequence-length tradeoffs; four, next steps and action items.
[00:36] Markus Voss: Sounds good. We're mainly interested in the 256 vs 1024 sequence workload since our customers vary.
[00:45] Owen Patel: Right, and we re-ran the 1k and 256 traces with continuous batching enabled plus prefix KV caching turned on. Note: some of the transcript notes mistranscribed KV cache as "KV cash" in the sheet.
[00:59] Lena Ortiz: Quick clarification — in the spreadsheet the TTFT column, is that measured from first request arrival to first token or first byte of streaming?
[01:05] Owen Patel: That's a good callout. TTFT there is first token emitted at the application boundary. Streaming first byte is typically 15–30ms later in our stack, depending on the route.
[01:15] Priya Khatri: Okay. So what were the baseline numbers?
[01:18] Owen Patel: Baseline from iteration 1 for the 1024 traces was averaging 420ms TTFT cold, warm was around 310ms. For 256 traces cold ~260ms, warm ~170ms.
[01:30] Lena Ortiz: And v3 after tuning?
[01:33] Owen Patel: v3 we saw cold 1024 down to 240–260ms with a kernel switch to the CUTLASS-path-optimized kernel and enabling int8 quant on the attention kernels. Warm 1024 hits ~180ms. For 256, cold dropped to ~140ms and warm under 90ms. The streaming L1 flush change reduced token gap by about 10–20ms per token.
[01:58] Markus Voss: Wait, int8 on attention — did you see any delta in output quality? That's a red line for us.
[02:05] Owen Patel: Minimal for this model family at the prompt lengths you run. We measured embeddings similarity on the eval set — average cosine delta was <0.006, which for your rerank/feedback loop is within noise. We can attach the eval deck.
[02:20] Lena Ortiz: Good to hear. Any quantization fallback if you see quality drift?
[02:24] Owen Patel: Yes — we recommend a canary route with the int8 paths and a fallback to fp16 for requests where your QA set metrics drop. The runtime supports per-request kernel selection so you can pin certain routes to fp16.
[02:35] Evan Zhou (joined): Sorry for the delay, bandwidth spiked. Quick Q: did you change batch sizes?
[02:40] Owen Patel: We reduced the micro-batch target to 4 for low-latency lanes and kept a throughput lane with batch=16 for burst; the routing policy demotes long-tail users to the throughput pool. That helped keep the TTFTs low for the 95th percentile.
[02:55] Priya Khatri: Can you explain the prefix caching change? We saw notes about trimming prefixes — what does that mean?
[03:02] Owen Patel: Sure. The pilot traces had long repeated system prompts. We enabled prefix eviction at 2k tokens and a delta-based hash so that repeated prefixes are served from KV cache bucket. Effectively we avoid re-computing key/value pairs for common prefixes; that shaves off ~40–60ms on cold for long-context calls.
[03:20] Lena Ortiz: In the logs we saw sometimes the server delayed streaming the first token by extra 80ms on long contexts. Is that what you mean by cold?
[03:26] Owen Patel: That's the prefix build time. When the KV cache misses you get a small synchronous perf hit while the KV is built; with the eviction threshold and the prefix hash optimization the miss rate dropped in our runs from 42% to 9% on your traces.
[03:39] Markus Voss: Any compliance/security impact on keeping the KV cache? We have sensitive PII in some prompts.
[03:46] Maya Chen: Good flag. The KV cache is ephemeral and memory-resident; for Redwood Dedicated/Private we also support encrypted in-memory storage and an optional no-cache policy per-customer. We can provide the architecture note.
[03:59] Lena Ortiz: Great. Now, kernel swap — you mentioned CUTLASS path? I'm not sure I caught that.
[04:06] Owen Patel: Yeah, sometimes transcribed as "cutlass" — it's the CUDA CUTLASS kernels tuned for this model's matmul sizes. We switched from the default fused attention kernel to a variant that has lower startup latency for shorter sequences. This helped TTFT especially on A100 pools.
[04:22] Priya Khatri: Is that available on our dedicated pool or only on hosted?
[04:26] Maya Chen: It's in both — depends on the container image and runtime tuning. For Dedicated we'd bake the optimized kernel set into your reserved image.
[04:33] Lena Ortiz: What about sequence length heuristics? Our traffic is mixed but tail calls at 1.5k tokens are common for power users.
[04:41] Owen Patel: For tails >1k, we recommend a separate route that allows longer KV construction windows and a slightly higher TTFT SLA; you can also configure a streaming-first token policy where we emit a partial system token earlier then backfill. That gives perceived latency improvements for users.
[04:56] Markus Voss: Backfill sounds complex. Any chance it confuses downstream parsers?
[05:00] Owen Patel: It can — we add an emission marker in the streaming frames so parsers can ignore backfill if they expect strict token order. We'll share the schema.
[05:08] Lena Ortiz: Alright, let's talk numbers for SLOs. If we aim for 200ms 95th for our chat endpoint at 256 median load, is that realistic?
[05:16] Owen Patel: With the tuned kernel + int8 + prefix cache + micro-batch=4 it's realistic in our lab for the 95th at 256, assuming load shaping and no noisy neighbors. In your Dedicated environment with reserved capacity, you'd see stable numbers; hosted can get similar but depends on concurrency.
[05:31] Evan Zhou: We need to see tail variance over a day. Can you provide a 24h runbook or we run the agent ourselves?
[05:36] Owen Patel: We'll provide a container image and a short script to replay your traces for 24 hours. Owen: action — I'll hand off the tuned container and a runbook.
[05:45] Maya Chen: Quick note — we also tested streaming chunk sizes; reducing chunk to 64 bytes helped with perceived TTFT on mobile, but increased CPU per-token slightly. Tradeoff you might choose in config.
[05:57] Priya Khatri: Any obvious risks we should flag to the execs?
[06:00] Daria Lopez: From CS perspective: quality drift risk with int8 (low), additional ops in runtime for backfill (medium), and possible infra ops to enable the cutlass kernels on-prem (low-medium). We'll document each.
[06:12] Lena Ortiz: Good — can we get a recommended default config to start the pilot with?
[06:16] Owen Patel: Yes — recommended default: sequence-limit=1024, int8_attention=true (canary), micro-batch-target=4 for low-latency lane, batching window 20ms, prefix-eviction=2048, streaming-chunk=64. We'll format that as YAML in the runbook.
[06:30] Markus Voss: Regarding monitoring, what metrics should we pull into our Grafana?
[06:34] Maya Chen: Token-emit-latency, KV-cache-hit-rate, kernel-path (fp16/int8) distribution, per-route TTFT pctiles, cpu/gpu utilization, and queue-wait-time.
[06:44] Lena Ortiz: Competitors — we ran a quick bench earlier and saw Anthropic endpoints gave consistent median but worse 95th, OpenAI had better single-token latency on small sequences but cost was 2.5x.
[06:56] Maya Chen: Good to document that in the competitive sheet.
[06:59] Priya Khatri: Anything else on cost? We care about unit token cost and committed capacity delta.
[07:04] Maya Chen: With Dedicated and these params, we estimate token unit cost down 18% from your hosted baseline due to the throughput lane and quantization. We'll attach the model for committed capacity pricing.
[07:14] Lena Ortiz: Can you walk through the failover policy if a node with the optimized kernel fails?
[07:19] Owen Patel: The runtime supports model-variant routing; if a node reports kernel mismatch, requests are routed to a fallback instance that runs the fp16 kernel. Failover is automated and we keep a warm pool for that.
[07:30] Evan Zhou: OK. For actionables, we'd like the tuned container, metrics dashboard template, and a 24h replay script.
[07:37] Maya Chen: We'll do that. Owen to provide container and replay, Maya to send pricing, Daria to send ops notes on security and kernel install.
[07:46] Priya Khatri: Timeline?
[07:48] Maya Chen: We'll aim to deliver the container + runbook in 3 business days, pricing same day, ops/security doc by EOD next Tue.
[07:57] Lena Ortiz: Great. Any blockers?
[08:00] Markus Voss: We need an IP whitelist for the replay agent. Evan will provide CIDR ranges.
[08:05] Evan Zhou: I'll share that after the call.
[08:08] Daria Lopez: I'll also add a note about SSO flow for the restricted console access in the ops doc.
[08:14] Maya Chen: Okay let's recap next steps, then we'll close.
[08:20] Owen Patel: Quick recaps on what I promised: 1) tuned container image + runbook; 2) 24h replay script + sample config; 3) YAML recommended defaults.
[08:30] Maya Chen: And I: pricing/committed capacity quote + short sales sheet, and I will include the competitive notes.
[08:36] Daria Lopez: I'll hand over security/kernel install notes and an SSO/console access checklist.
[08:40] Lena Ortiz: We'll run the 24h replay and feed logs back by next Friday.
[08:45] Markus Voss: We'll also schedule the infra dry-run for kernel installation with Redwood next Tue.
[08:50] Maya Chen: Perfect. Thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with attachments.
[08:55] Meeting ended.

Notes on transcription imperfections: some proper nouns were transcribed inconsistently (CUTLASS vs cutlass), and several technical terms like KV cache/KV cash, TTFT spelled out or abbreviated variably.
